title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #603: Find the smallest cardinal $C$ such that any family $(A_i)$ of countably infinite sets with $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 2$ for all $i \neq j$ can be $C$-colored so no $A_i$ is monochromatic. The problem is **OPEN** — known bounds are $2 \leq C \leq \aleph_0$ but the exact value is unknown. Attributed to Komjáth, recorded in Erdős's [Er87] compilation.
mathContext: The problem asks for $\sup \{ \chi(\mathcal{A}) : \mathcal{A} \text{ is a valid family} \}$ where $\chi(\mathcal{A})$ is the minimum number of colors to break monochromaticity. The analogous problem with $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 1$ was solved by Komjáth ($C = \aleph_0$).

title: Set Family Definitions
content: `IsCountablyInfiniteFamily A` requires each $A_i$ to be both `Set.Countable` and `Set.Infinite` — this is the natural class of 'small infinite' sets. `IntersectionNot2 A` formalizes $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 2$ for $i \neq j$ using `Set.ncard`, which returns a natural number (0 for infinite sets). The combined `IsValidFamily` bundles both constraints.
mathContext: The constraint $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 2$ is stated via `Set.ncard` rather than `Finset.card`, avoiding the need to prove intersections are finite. Since `ncard` returns 0 for infinite sets, the constraint automatically allows infinite intersections.

title: Coloring Definitions
content: `IsMonochromatic S c` holds when $\exists$ color such that $c(x) = $ color for all $x \in S$. `IsValidColoring A c` requires that no $A_i$ is monochromatic under $c$. This is the 'weak' coloring condition — contrast with 'strong' (rainbow) coloring where all elements of each set must have distinct colors.
mathContext: A coloring $c : \alpha \to \Gamma$ is valid iff $\forall i, \exists x, y \in A_i$ with $c(x) \neq c(y)$. For infinite sets, this is equivalent to: no $A_i$ is contained in a single color class $c^{-1}(\gamma)$.

title: Chromatic Number
content: `SufficientColors A C` asserts $\exists \Gamma$ with $|\Gamma| \leq C$ and a valid coloring $c : \alpha \to \Gamma$. The `chromaticNumber` takes the infimum over all sufficient cardinals using `Cardinal.sInf`. Note the use of `Cardinal.mk` to convert types to their cardinality, and `Cardinal.le` for the comparison — cardinal arithmetic in Lean requires careful use of universe levels.
mathContext: The chromatic number $\chi(\mathcal{A}) = \inf\{C : \exists \Gamma, |\Gamma| \leq C, \exists c : \alpha \to \Gamma \text{ valid}\}$. The problem asks for $C^* = \sup_{\mathcal{A} \text{ valid}} \chi(\mathcal{A})$.

title: The Main Conjecture
content: ErdosConjecture603(C): for all valid families, C colors suffice. minimalChromatic: the smallest such C.
mathContext: The question is the value of minimalChromatic.

title: Komjath's Theorem
content: `komjath_not1` axiomatizes Komjáth's theorem: for families with $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 1$, $\aleph_0$ colors suffice. This is declared as an `axiom` because the proof requires deep set-theoretic arguments beyond current Mathlib. The contrast with the $\neq 2$ case (still open) is the central motivation for Problem #603.
mathContext:
Komjáth proved: if $(A_i)$ is a family of countably infinite sets with $|A_i \cap A_j| 
eq 1$ for all $i 
eq j$, then $ igcup A_i$ can be $\aleph_0$-colored so no $A_i$ is monochromatic. The proof uses a transfinite induction argument specific to the $
eq 1$ constraint.

title: Bounds
content: `lower_bound_2` proves $C \geq 2$ by contradiction: with $< 2$ colors, any infinite set is automatically monochromatic (has a `sorry` for the cardinal $< 2$ case analysis). `countable_suffices_trivial` axiomatizes the trivial upper bound: assign each element a distinct natural number color, so no infinite set can be monochromatic. Together these give $2 \leq C \leq \aleph_0$.
mathContext: Lower bound: with $|\Gamma| < 2$, pigeonhole forces any infinite set to have all elements the same color. Upper bound: the identity coloring $c(x) = x$ (after injection into $\mathbb{N}$) gives $\aleph_0$ colors with no monochromatic infinite set.

title: Finite vs Infinite
content: CanDoBetterThanAleph0: some finite n suffices. Aleph0Necessary: no finite n works.
mathContext: The key open question: is the answer finite or infinite?

title: Hypergraph Perspective
content: `SetFamilyHypergraph` packages the set family as a hypergraph with vertices $V = \bigcup A_i$ and hyperedges $\mathcal{E} = \{A_i\}_{i \in I}$. The `weakChromatic` number (= `hypergraphChromatic`) is the minimum colors to break monochromaticity. This reformulation connects Problem #603 to the classical theory of Property B (Bernstein, 1908; Erdős-Hajnal, 1966): a hypergraph has Property B if it admits a 2-coloring with no monochromatic edge.
mathContext: The weak chromatic number $\chi_w(H) = \inf\{k : H \text{ has a proper } k\text{-coloring}\}$. For 2-uniform hypergraphs (= graphs), this is the ordinary chromatic number. For $\omega$-uniform hypergraphs (all edges infinite), Property B always holds (i.e., $\chi_w = 2$) for finite families, but not necessarily for infinite ones.

title: Disjoint Families
content: `disjoint_2_colors` (has `sorry`): if $A_i \cap A_j = \emptyset$ for all $i \neq j$, then 2 colors suffice. The proof idea: for disjoint infinite sets, color half of each set one color and half the other. This is the easiest special case — the difficulty in #603 comes from families where intersections exist but avoid size 2.
mathContext: Disjoint families vacuously satisfy $|A_i \cap A_j| \neq 2$ (since $|\emptyset| = 0 \neq 2$). The 2-coloring uses the fact that each infinite set can be split into two infinite subsets.

title: Satisfying Both Constraints
content: SatisfiesBoth: intersection != 1 AND != 2. both_constraints: Komjath's bound applies.
mathContext: Families avoiding both 1 and 2 are covered by Komjath's result.

title: Formal Statement
content: `erdos_603_statement` proves the formal equivalence: $\exists C, \text{ErdosConjecture603}(C)$ iff $\exists C, \forall \mathcal{A}$ valid, $C$ suffices for $\mathcal{A}$. This is essentially unfolding the definition — the proof is a straightforward `constructor` with both directions wrapping/unwrapping the `IsValidFamily` conjunction. The theorem confirms the formalization correctly captures the intended mathematical statement.
mathContext: The formal statement unfolds to: $\exists C, \forall \alpha\, I\, (A : I \to \text{Set}\,\alpha), (\text{countably infinite family} \wedge |A_i \cap A_j| \neq 2) \to \exists \Gamma\, (|\Gamma| \leq C) \, (c : \alpha \to \Gamma)$ valid.

title: Problem Status
content: The problem is OPEN. Known: 2 <= C <= aleph_0. For != 1: C = aleph_0 (Komjath). For != 2: unknown.
mathContext: The contrast with the solved != 1 case is notable.
